The OpenAPI schema is generated dynamically at runtime via drf_spectacular.SpectacularAPIView (cache_page 1h) — contract findings below are based on comparing code behavior (actual response shapes, actual error envelopes) against what @extend_schema/AutoSchema would document, not against a stored spec file.
Sub-agent verified these correctly reject repeat calls via INVALID_STAGE_TRANSITION rather than duplicating — no issue found there, in contrast to assign_placement (Finding ops-04).

findings.title: EmployeeStatusViewSet.history: unguarded int(employee_id) on query param can 500

evidence.note: Line 361-366: `employee_id = request.query_params.get('employee_id'); if not employee_id: return 400`. This only rejects an empty/missing value. Line 382: `queryset = self.service.get_employee_status_history(employee_id=int(employee_id), ...)` — a non-numeric string like `?employee_id=abc` passes the falsy check and reaches a bare `int()` cast, raising ValueError uncaught by the view, producing an unhandled 500 instead of the 400 the sibling date-parsing block (lines 372-379) already demonstrates is the intended pattern for this same action.

recommendation.text: Wrap int(employee_id) in the same try/except ValueError -> 400 pattern already used for start_date/end_date in this same method (lines 372-379).

findings.title: EmployeeStatusViewSet.planned: unguarded int(employee_id) on query param can 500

evidence.note: Same pattern as Finding RAW-00000001-0: `if not employee_id: return 400` (lines 419-423) then `int(employee_id)` used twice unguarded (lines 426 and 429) to fetch current/planned statuses. A non-numeric employee_id (e.g. 'abc') raises an uncaught ValueError -> 500.

recommendation.text: Validate employee_id is numeric before calling int(), returning 400 with a clear message on failure (mirrors fix for RAW-00000001-0).

findings.title: EmployeeStatusViewSet.division_headcount: unguarded int(division_id) on query param can 500

evidence.note: Lines 505-509 reject only a missing/empty division_id. Line 520: `division_id=int(division_id)` is unguarded — a non-numeric division_id raises an uncaught ValueError -> 500, same class of bug as history/planned.

recommendation.text: Validate division_id is numeric before calling int(), returning 400 on failure.

findings.title: get_division_headcount silently returns all-zero 200 for a non-existent division_id instead of 404/400

evidence.note: Lines 650-654 filter StaffUnit by division_id with no existence check on Division. A bogus/nonexistent division_id yields an empty staff_units queryset, so the endpoint returns 200 with total_count=0, in_service_count=0, absent_count=0 rather than surfacing that the division does not exist — a client typo in division_id is indistinguishable from a legitimately empty division.

recommendation.text: Look up Division.objects.get(pk=division_id) first (as get_absence_statistics already does at line 718) and return 404/400 on DoesNotExist for consistency with the sibling endpoint.

findings.title: StatusDocumentViewSet documented in code but its route is commented out in urls.py

evidence.note: views.py's StatusDocumentViewSet docstring (lines 587-594, sha256 cf7631af7471955504dfcb6240dd4079d3e22b0ff083a7e3794c97ff40439bc3) states 'GET /status-documents/ - Список документов' and 'GET /status-documents/{id}/'. urls.py line 7 has `# router.register(r'status-documents', StatusDocumentViewSet, basename='status-document')` commented out — the endpoint documented in the class docstring does not exist on the live route table. Documents remain reachable only nested under EmployeeStatusDetailSerializer.documents, not via this dedicated read endpoint.

recommendation.text: Either uncomment the registration if the standalone document listing endpoint is needed, or remove the stale docstring claims to avoid client/consumer confusion.

findings.title: Custom error envelope on statuses create/extend/terminate/cancel/upload_document not documented via @extend_schema

evidence.note: create() returns a bespoke `{'error': str, 'errors': [str,...]}` 400 body on ValidationError (lines 120-131); extend/terminate/cancel/upload_document return `{'error': str(e)}` (lines 257-258, 283-284, 307-308, 335-336). None of these five actions carries an @extend_schema decorator, unlike history/planned (lines 338-350, 391-402) which do document their 200 response. drf-spectacular's AutoSchema will infer only the happy-path 2xx shape from the serializer for the undocumented actions, so the actual 400 error contract is invisible in the generated OpenAPI schema for the majority of this ViewSet's write actions.

recommendation.text: Add @extend_schema(responses={..., 400: <error envelope schema>}) to create/extend/terminate/cancel/upload_document to match the coverage already given to history/planned.

findings.title: apps/employees EmployeeViewSet (create/transfer/dismiss/history) is not wired into any URLconf

evidence.note: `# path("api/employees/", include("organization_management.apps.employees.api.urls")),` is commented out, and grep confirms apps.employees.api.urls is included nowhere else. apps/core/api/urls.py line 15 registers a DIFFERENT, read-only EmployeeViewSet (viewsets.ReadOnlyModelViewSet, apps/core/api/views.py) at /api/core/employees/ instead. The employees app's own EmployeeViewSet — with its create/transfer/dismiss/history write actions and the defects catalogued in Findings RAW-00000008-0 through RAW-00000011-0 below — is currently dead code with no HTTP route. This is itself worth flagging: it is a maintained-looking, docstring-annotated ViewSet that a developer could reasonably assume is live, and it will resurface its latent bugs the moment someone re-enables the route.

recommendation.text: Either delete apps/employees/api if superseded by apps/core's read-only EmployeeViewSet, or fix and re-enable it deliberately — do not leave a route commented out indefinitely with unreviewed defects inside.

findings.title: employees.transfer creates an audit-trail row and commits it even when the zone-restricted permission check denies the transfer

evidence.note: Inside `with transaction.atomic():` (line 129), `EmployeeTransferHistory.objects.create(...)` (lines 132-141) runs UNCONDITIONALLY, before the DIRECTORATE_HEAD/DIVISION_HEAD zone checks at lines 148-157. Those checks `return Response({'detail': ...}, status=403)` directly inside the atomic block — a `return` exits the context manager without raising, so Django's atomic() COMMITS on normal exit. The actual employee.division_id/position_id reassignment (lines 159-163) happens after the checks and is correctly skipped on denial, but the EmployeeTransferHistory row recording the attempted transfer is persisted regardless — a denied, out-of-zone transfer leaves a committed audit record implying a transfer took place. Lines 152 and 156 also do an unguarded `int(division_id)` cast on the same request field, so a non-numeric division_id raises inside the atomic block and (correctly, this time, because it's a real exception) rolls back — but returns an unhandled 500 rather than 400.

recommendation.text: Move the permission/zone check before EmployeeTransferHistory.objects.create(), and validate division_id/position_id as integers via a serializer before use.

findings.title: employees.perform_create bare except swallows failures to create the employee's initial status

evidence.note: Lines 76-86: `try: EmployeeStatus.objects.create(...) except Exception: pass`. Any failure — a full_clean() ValidationError, a DB constraint violation, a None hire_date — is silently discarded, leaving a newly created WORKING employee with no active status. This directly contradicts the documented invariant in obsidian-vault/Personnel-Records/Decisions.md ('Статус по умолчанию каждому работающему сотруднику'), which is otherwise enforced via apps/statuses/services.ensure_active_status — this orphaned code path duplicates that responsibility without any of its safeguards or logging.

recommendation.text: Replace the bare except with a narrow catch that logs the failure, or delegate initial-status creation entirely to statuses.services.ensure_active_status so there is one owner of the invariant.

findings.title: employees.history action is a stub that always returns an empty list regardless of the requested employee

evidence.note: `def history(self, request, pk=None): """Получение истории переводов сотрудника.""" # ... (логика получения истории) return Response({'history': []})` — the docstring promises transfer history, but the body is a placeholder that ignores pk entirely and never queries EmployeeTransferHistory (the model the transfer action itself writes to).

recommendation.text: Implement the query against EmployeeTransferHistory filtered by employee=pk, or remove the endpoint until implemented.

findings.title: employees.dismiss assigns raw request data to a DateField and saves directly, bypassing serializer validation

evidence.note: Line 176: `employee.dismissal_date = request.data.get('dismissal_date')` is assigned directly to the model instance with no format check, then `employee.save(update_fields=['employment_status', 'dismissal_date'])` (line 177) bypasses any serializer/full_clean(). A malformed date string (e.g. 'not-a-date') would only be caught at the database adapter layer on save, which is not wrapped in a try/except here — a plausible unhandled 500 on malformed input on the dismissal golden path. (This action's side effects are otherwise properly gated by statuses/signals.py::close_statuses_on_dismissal, which correctly falls back to today's date when dismissal_date is None.)

recommendation.text: Validate dismissal_date through a small serializer (DateField) before assignment, returning 400 on a parse failure instead of letting a DB-layer error surface as 500.

findings.title: employees.get_permissions comments claim role-restricted actions but every branch grants identical IsAuthenticated-only access

evidence.note: Comments say 'Прием/увольнение: Роль-4 и Роль-5' (line 94), 'Перевод: Роль-4, Роль-5; а также Роль-3/6 в своей зоне' (line 97), 'Редактирование: Роль-4/5 и Роль-3/6 в своей зоне' (line 102) — but every one of the four branches sets `self.permission_classes = [permissions.IsAuthenticated]` with no role/DRF-permission-class differentiation at all. The only actual role enforcement anywhere in this ViewSet is the ad-hoc zone check inside transfer() (lines 148-157, see RAW-00000008-0) — create, destroy, dismiss, and update/partial_update have no role gate whatsoever despite the comments implying one exists.

recommendation.text: Either implement real role-based permission classes matching the comments, or remove the misleading comments so reviewers don't assume RBAC is enforced here.

evidence.note: `if int(row.get("need", 0)) < 1:` — row.get(...,0) only substitutes 0 when the 'need' key is absent; a client sending `{"need": "abc"}` or `{"need": null}` (key present) reaches `int()` directly and raises ValueError/TypeError, uncaught. Reached via POST /api/ops/security-events/{id}/demand/approve/ and PATCH /api/ops/security-events/{id}/recon/ — both on the event-creation golden path. apps/operations/api/exception_handler.py's ops_exception_handler only wraps DomainError/known IntegrityError constraints, so this ValueError falls through to Django's raw 500 with no error_code/request_id envelope the client's parser expects — a genuine contract gap, not just a crash. (Identified via sub-agent static trace of security_events.py.)

recommendation.text: Validate 'need' is a parseable positive integer as part of field_errors validation (alongside sector/task/group checks in the same loop) rather than casting directly in the conditional.

evidence.note: `allocated = int(allocated_count)` where allocated_count=data.get("allocatedCount", 0) — an explicit `{"allocatedCount": null}` or a non-numeric string crashes the same way as RAW-00000013-0, reached via PATCH /api/ops/security-events/{id}/forces/{request_id}/, before any validation branch runs. (Identified via sub-agent static trace.)

recommendation.text: Validate allocatedCount is a parseable non-negative integer before casting, returning a 400 field error on failure.

findings.title: ops passport._validate_sectors_payload: .get() on a non-dict list element raises AttributeError

evidence.note: `name = str((sector or {}).get("name", ""))` guards only a falsy/None sector, not a non-dict truthy value. PATCH /api/ops/objects/{id}/passport/ with `{"sectors": ["not-a-dict"]}` makes `sector or {}` evaluate to the string itself, and `.get()` on a str raises AttributeError, uncaught — same missing-exception-contract gap as RAW-00000013-0/014-0. The same 'assume list item is always a dict' pattern recurs in the approve_demand/update_recon row loops. (Identified via sub-agent static trace.)

recommendation.text: Type-check each row/sector element (isinstance(x, dict)) before calling .get(), rejecting non-dict entries as a field error.

findings.title: ops security_events.assign_placement: retrying the same postId/employeeId assignment is not deduplicated

evidence.note: The only duplicate guard present rejects the SAME employee being assigned to a DIFFERENT post (lines 592-600: `a.get("employeeId") == employee_key and a.get("postId") != post_id`). There is no check that post_id is already assigned — to the same employee or a different one — before `event.placement_assignments = [*event.placement_assignments, assignment]` (line 635) unconditionally appends. A client retry of POST /api/ops/security-events/{id}/placement/assign/ with the same postId/employeeId (the classic timeout-then-retry idempotent-POST scenario) creates a second assignment row for the same post/employee pair; complete_acknowledgement (lines 828-833) requires every entry in placement_assignments to be individually acknowledged, so a silent duplicate can block stage completion until the ghost duplicate is separately acknowledged. Cross-checked tests/test_ops_security_events_api.py (lines 395-424 test cross-post double-assignment of the same employee, not same-post re-assignment) — confirmed no test covers this path. (Identified via sub-agent static trace + test-suite grep.)

recommendation.text: Add a duplicate-post guard alongside the existing duplicate-employee guard (reject or no-op when postId already has an active, non-unassigned entry), matching the idempotency the retry scenario requires.

findings.title: ops SecurityEventViewSet.list page_size query param has no upper bound and always materializes the full table first

evidence.note: `page_size = max(int(request.query_params.get("page_size", "20")), 1)` is floored at 1 but never capped — `?page_size=999999` returns every row in one response. Line 238 (`rows = list(OpsSecurityEvent.objects.all())`) always fully materializes the entire table into Python memory regardless of the requested page, before any slicing happens. This ViewSet is a plain viewsets.ViewSet and never calls self.paginate_queryset(), so the project's DEFAULT_PAGINATION_CLASS (StandardResultsSetPagination, max_page_size=1000) does not apply here. Also `int(request.query_params.get("page_size", "20"))` is itself an unguarded cast — a non-numeric page_size raises ValueError uncaught. (Identified via sub-agent static trace; sampled ~8 of 39 list() implementations in this file — DutyShiftViewSet.list, OpsPersonnelViewSet.list, bindable_objects, OpsDailyEmployeesViewSet.list, OpsDailySubmissionsViewSet.list all similarly build hand-rolled {"results": [...]} envelopes with no page/limit params at all, always returning the complete queryset.)

recommendation.text: Cap page_size at a sane maximum (matching StandardResultsSetPagination's max_page_size=1000 for consistency) and validate it's numeric before casting; audit the other unpaginated list() implementations named above for the same issue and either paginate them or document why the registry sizes involved make it a non-issue (as was already done, correctly, for SecurityObjectViewSet — see inventory).

findings.title: apps/ops has zero @extend_schema/drf-spectacular annotations; hand-rolled envelope shapes are invisible to the generated OpenAPI schema

evidence.note: grep -rn 'extend_schema' across the whole ops app returns nothing. DEFAULT_SCHEMA_CLASS is drf_spectacular.openapi.AutoSchema (config/settings/base.py:172), which infers schema from serializers/views with zero manual annotation. Because SecurityObjectViewSet.list (lines 91-117) and SecurityEventViewSet.list and most other ops list()/action methods are plain viewsets.ViewSet methods returning raw Response(dict) — e.g. {"results":..., "freshness":..., "kpi":..., "freshnessPolicy":..., "unavailableKpi":...} — AutoSchema has no serializer to introspect for these, so these hand-written envelope shapes exist only in code comments and the frontend's hand-written parser, with zero machine-checkable OpenAPI documentation. (Identified via sub-agent static trace.)

recommendation.text: Add @extend_schema(responses=...) with an OpenApiTypes/inline serializer describing the actual envelope for each hand-rolled ops response, at least for the highest-traffic endpoints (SecurityEventViewSet.list, SecurityObjectViewSet.list).

findings.title: No API versioning scheme in use across the whole backend

evidence.note: No DEFAULT_VERSIONING_CLASS in REST_FRAMEWORK settings (config/settings/base.py), no /v1/ URL segment anywhere in config/urls.py or any app's urls.py, no Accept-header versioning scheme. Every app (common/operations/core/documents/ops/staff_unit/statuses/secondments/reports/notifications/audit/dictionaries/divisions) is mounted directly under /api/<app>/ with no version prefix.

recommendation.text: not_applicable — flagged only as an architectural note per the audit brief; not a defect on its own given this is a single-consumer internal system (one frontend, no external API contract to preserve across versions).
